intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera, stopping at the Red Beach and White Beach for swimming and snorkeling. The evening departure lets you enjoy the world-famous Oia sunset from the water while avoiding the intense midday heat. Light snacks and local wine are typically included. Indoor alternative: visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira if weather turns.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches enclosed by towering white cliffs. Arrive before the crowds and midday heat for the best experience. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and explore the famous rusted shipwreck. Indoor alternative: visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos in the afternoon.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete
experiences.description: Join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and kalitsounia (cheese pastries) using locally sourced ingredients. Enjoy your creations for lunch with local raki. Held indoors or under shaded pergolas, ideal for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach at sunrise or early morning when the lagoon is calm, uncrowded, and the light is magical. Snorkel through the shallow turquoise lagoon teeming with sea life and explore the small islet connected by a sandbar. Rent snorkel gear locally for a minimal cost. Indoor alternative for midday: explore the nearby Chrysoskalitissa Monastery, a cool stone structure with cultural significance.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Explore the atmospheric streets, browse souvenir stalls, and soak in your first views of the Acropolis lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near the airport or on arrival in Athens (€2–3)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna in Psiri — try souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and a Greek salad for around €8–10. Look for spots packed with locals rather than tourists.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is short due to afternoon arrival. Prioritize rest and orientation. Buy a rechargeable Ath.ena transit card at the airport Metro station for cheaper travel around Athens.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (Acropolis + surrounding sites) costs €30 but is well worth it — valid for 5 days across multiple sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for budget souvenirs and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Thissio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the pedestrian promenade. Enjoy the golden hour atmosphere before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) or spanakopita from a local bakery near your hostel — €1.50–2
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyros wrap from a street stand near Monastiraki (€2.50–3.50)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna dinner in Thissio or Psiri — moussaka or pastitsio with a carafe of house wine, around €10–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Acropolis involves uneven marble surfaces. Bring water and sunscreen. The combined Acropolis ticket saves money if you plan to visit multiple ancient sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums) — entry is €12. Spend 2–3 hours exploring ancient Greek artifacts, the Antikythera Mechanism, and stunning gold Mycenaean treasures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian quarter with street art, independent cafes, and a very local vibe. Visit the colorful Strefi Hill park for panoramic city views at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Kolonaki, Athens' upscale neighborhood, for window shopping and people-watching. Take the Lycabettus Hill funicular (€7 return) for spectacular 360° views of Athens and the Acropolis at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor — €0.50, plus Greek coffee at a local kafeneio (€1.50)
meals.lunch: Eat at a laiki (street market) if one is running nearby, or find a neighborhood psistaria (grill house) for a budget plate — €6–8
meals.dinner: Try fasolada (bean soup) or gemista (stuffed vegetables) at a traditional ouzeri in Exarchia — filling and very affordable at €7–9

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays — check the day of the week and adjust if needed. Exarchia is lively and authentic but stay aware of your surroundings in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early Metro + tram to Glyfada or Vouliagmeni beach on the Athens Riviera — about 45–60 minutes from central Athens. Vouliagmeni has a stunning natural lake (€15 entry) or free public beach sections nearby. Enjoy a morning swim in the clear Aegean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at the beach or explore the coastal promenade. Rent a sunbed if desired (€5–8) or bring your own towel and find a free spot. The water temperature in June is perfect — around 22–24°C.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by tram/Metro. Head to the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) area in the evening for a lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from a bakery before heading out — cheese pie and juice, €2–3
meals.lunch: Beach taverna lunch — grilled fish of the day or calamari with salad and bread, €12–15 (a slight splurge for the beach experience)
meals.dinner: Eat at a no-frills taverna near the Central Market — fresh grilled sardines or a mixed meze plate, €8–10

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera beaches are easily accessible by public transport — take Metro Line 2 to Syntagma then the tram toward Voula/Vouliagmeni. Bring cash as some beach vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early morning ferry from Piraeus port to Aegina island — one of the closest and most affordable Greek islands (ferry ticket €8–10 each way, journey ~1 hour). Arrive and rent a bicycle (€5–8/day) to explore the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to the stunning Temple of Aphaia (€6 entry) — one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples with panoramic sea views. Then head to Agia Marina beach on the east coast for a refreshing swim in turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegina Town in the late afternoon. Browse the colorful harbor, try local pistachios (Aegina is famous for them — buy a bag for €3–5), then catch the evening ferry back to Piraeus.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing or grab something at Piraeus port — coffee and pastry, €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a harbor taverna in Aegina Town — grilled octopus or fish soup with bread, €10–13
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — grab a souvlaki wrap or eat at your hostel's communal kitchen to save money after a full day, €3–5

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance at the Blue Star Ferries or Hellenic Seaways websites. The first ferry from Piraeus is usually around 7:00–8:00 AM. Piraeus is reachable from central Athens via Metro Line 1 (Green Line).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the KTEL bus from Athens (Kifissos Bus Terminal) to Nafplio in the Peloponnese — about 2.5 hours, ticket ~€13. Check into a budget guesthouse in Nafplio's charming old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful Venetian old town on foot — one of Greece's most picturesque towns. Visit the Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) by climbing the famous 999 steps for breathtaking views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront promenade and through the neoclassical streets of the old town. Watch the sunset from Acronauplia (the lower castle, free to walk around).

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing Athens or at the bus terminal — coffee and koulouri, €2
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite after arriving in Nafplio — gyros or a cheese pie from a local bakery, €3–4
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional taverna in Nafplio's old town — try the local specialty of lamb with orzo (arni me kritharaki), €10–12

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is a great base for exploring the Peloponnese. Book your guesthouse in advance as it's a popular destination. The Palamidi steps are steep — go in the morning or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi (€10–15 shared) to Epidaurus to visit the ancient Theatre of Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world with remarkable acoustics. Entry is €12 (combined with the museum).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and head to Karathona Beach — a lovely sandy beach just a 20-minute walk from the old town (or short taxi ride). Enjoy the calm, clear waters of the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Nafplio for a leisurely evening. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar with Acropolis views (just a drink — budget €4–6 for a local beer or wine).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse if included, or a local bakery — tiropita and coffee, €2.50
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the local market — olives, feta, bread, tomatoes, and fruit — €4–5 total
meals.dinner: Try a psarotaverna (fish taverna) near the waterfront — grilled sea bream or sea bass with vegetables, €12–14

day_by_day.notes: Epidaurus also hosts a famous summer festival of ancient drama — check if any performances coincide with your visit (tickets from €15). The beach at Karathona is free with no facilities, so bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Nafplio to Santorini: Take the KTEL bus back to Athens (or to Piraeus directly), then board an afternoon high-speed ferry to Santorini. Alternatively, take a direct ferry from Nafplio area ports. High-speed ferry from Piraeus to Santorini takes ~5 hours (€40–55 economy).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini (Thira) at the port of Athinios. Take the local bus (€1.80) up to Fira, the island's capital. Check into a budget hostel or studio apartment in Fira or nearby Karterados (cheaper than Oia).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Fira on foot — walk along the caldera edge for stunning views, browse the main street, and get oriented on the island.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — bakery items, €2–3
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or pack snacks for the journey — sandwiches and fruit, €3–5
meals.dinner: First dinner in Santorini — find a local taverna away from the main tourist strip in Fira for more reasonable prices. Try fava (yellow split pea dip) and tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), local Santorini specialties, €10–12

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is the most expensive part of this itinerary. Save money by staying in Fira or Karterados rather than Oia, eating at local spots away from the caldera-view restaurants, and using the island's public bus system (KTEL Santorini) instead of taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Perissa or Perivolos beach on the south coast — famous for their black volcanic sand. Arrive early to claim a good spot. The beach is free; sunbeds cost €5–8 if desired.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the beach. The black sand gets very hot in the afternoon sun — bring sandals. Swim in the crystal-clear blue Aegean. Walk along the long beach promenade connecting Perissa and Perivolos.
day_by_day.evening: Take the bus back to Fira. Walk the famous caldera path from Fira toward Imerovigli for spectacular sunset views — this is free and arguably better than the crowded Oia sunset spot.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry from a local bakery in Fira before heading to the beach — €2.50
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perissa — fresh calamari, Greek salad, and a cold Mythos beer, €12–15
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira at a non-caldera-view restaurant — souvlaki plate or moussaka, €9–11. The caldera-view restaurants charge 2–3x more for the same food.

day_by_day.notes: The black sand beaches of Santorini are unique but the sand gets extremely hot — water shoes or sandals are essential. Perissa has more budget-friendly options than the northern beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€15–25/day) to explore the island independently. Drive to the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by volcanic ash (entry €12). Often called the 'Greek Pompeii.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Red Beach near Akrotiri — one of Santorini's most dramatic and unique beaches with towering red volcanic cliffs. Then continue to the village of Megalochori or Pyrgos for a more authentic, less touristy Santorini experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive up to Pyrgos village (the highest point on the island) for panoramic 360° views and a quieter sunset experience than Oia. Explore the medieval castle ruins at the top.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or a local cafe — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, €3–4
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch bought from a local mini-market — bread, local Santorini cherry tomatoes, feta, olives, €4–5
meals.dinner: Dinner in Megalochori or Pyrgos village — authentic local taverna with fewer tourists and lower prices, €9–11

day_by_day.notes: Renting a scooter requires a valid license. If uncomfortable on a scooter, rent an ATV instead — no license required in Greece for small ATVs, though always ride carefully on the winding island roads. Red Beach has a short rocky path to access — wear sturdy shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Oia village in the morning (before the crowds arrive). Explore the iconic blue-domed churches, white-washed buildings, and narrow alleyways. Photography is stunning in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the famous caldera trail from Oia back toward Fira (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) — one of the most scenic hikes in Greece with breathtaking views the entire way. Alternatively, take the bus back and relax at Kamari beach.
day_by_day.evening: If you did the hike, you'll arrive back in Fira in time for the famous Oia sunset (take the bus back up). Join the crowds at Oia's castle ruins for the legendary Santorini sunset — arrive 1 hour early for a good spot.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before heading to Oia — coffee and tiropita, €2.50
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the hike or stop at a small cafe along the trail — sandwich and water, €4–6
meals.dinner: Farewell Santorini dinner — treat yourself slightly with a meal at a mid-range restaurant in Fira with caldera views, €15–18. Order the local white wine (Assyrtiko) — Santorini's famous grape variety.

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia caldera hike is moderately challenging. Wear good shoes, bring plenty of water (2+ liters), sunscreen, and a hat. Start early to avoid the worst of the midday heat. The trail is well-marked.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Santorini. Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira (€6) to see artifacts from the Akrotiri excavations, including stunning Minoan frescoes. Then do any last-minute shopping — local products like Santorini wine, fava, and capers make great budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the afternoon high-speed ferry back to Piraeus/Athens (book in advance for best prices — €40–55 economy). Enjoy the sea views and relax on the journey back.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Athens (Piraeus) in the evening. Take the Metro back to central Athens. Check into your Athens accommodation for the final night. Take a nostalgic last walk through Monastiraki and Plaka.

meals.breakfast: Final Santorini breakfast — Greek yogurt with local honey and fresh fruit at a cafe, €4–5
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or pack snacks — sandwiches and local snacks bought from a mini-market, €4–6
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — revisit your favorite taverna from Day 2 or try something new in Psiri. Budget €10–12 for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book your return ferry well in advance, especially for summer travel. High-speed ferries (SeaJets, Hellenic Seaways) are faster but pricier than conventional ferries — balance cost vs. time. Keep your transit card topped up for the Metro from Piraeus.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Revisit any sites you missed or simply enjoy a slow Greek breakfast at a neighborhood cafe. Visit the Zappeion Gardens or the National Garden (free) for a peaceful green escape in the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Monastiraki flea market — pick up olive oil, herbs, local honey, or handmade ceramics at reasonable prices. Head to the airport with plenty of time (allow 2–3 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, ancient history, and incredible Greek food!

meals.breakfast: Slow final Greek breakfast — freddo espresso (iced coffee), koulouri, and a cheese pie at a traditional kafeneio, €3–4
meals.lunch: Last souvlaki wrap in Athens — the perfect budget farewell meal, €2.50–3.50
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Athens Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) is connected to the city center by Metro Line 3 (Blue Line) — journey takes about 40 minutes and costs €9. Allow extra time for check-in and security. Use any remaining euros on last food or souvenirs at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Athens International Airport at 14:50 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at Athens Eleftherios Venizelos Airport at 14:50. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens (~40 min, budget-friendly). Check into your Athens accommodation near Monastiraki or Syntagma. Freshen up and take a relaxed stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Flea Market to get your bearings and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the charming Plaka neighborhood — the old town beneath the Acropolis. Enjoy the illuminated Acropolis views from street level. Explore the narrow, bougainvillea-lined streets at a leisurely pace.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki (€3–5) after settling in
meals.dinner: Dinner at Taverna tou Psara in Plaka — a classic mid-range taverna with grilled fish, moussaka, and local wine (€20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage light for the metro ride. Book accommodation in central Athens (Monastiraki, Syntagma, or Koukaki areas) for easy access to sights. Exchange some euros at the airport or use ATMs in the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — join the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) guided food tour starting around 9:00 AM. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local cheeses with a knowledgeable local guide. Sample traditional Greek products including loukoumades, local honey, and cured meats.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, visit the nearby Monastiraki Flea Market for browsing antiques and souvenirs. Then head to the Ancient Agora of Athens (€10 entry) — the heart of ancient Athenian civic life, featuring the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head up to Anafiotika, a tiny Cycladic-style village hidden within Plaka, for sunset views. Then explore the lively Psiri neighborhood for evening drinks and mezedes.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast included or offered during the food tour — Greek coffee and tiropita (cheese pie) from a local bakery near the market
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional ouzeri near the Central Market — try grilled octopus, taramasalata, and fresh bread with a glass of ouzo (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) in Psiri neighborhood — order a spread of small plates: tzatziki, dolmades, saganaki, and grilled lamb chops (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Athens Central Market Food Tour in advance as spots fill up. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover significant ground. The Ancient Agora combo ticket also covers the Kerameikos archaeological site if you want to extend the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. The morning light is spectacular for photos. Combined ticket (€20) includes the Acropolis Museum — visit the museum afterward, which houses original sculptures and artifacts from the site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the Acropolis Museum (included in combo ticket) — one of the finest archaeological museums in the world. Afterward, walk to the Panathenaic Stadium (Kallimarmaro) — the original Olympic stadium built entirely of marble, free to view from outside or €5 to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views from Filopappou Hill (free, 10-minute walk from the Acropolis) — arguably the best panoramic view of the Acropolis and Athens skyline. Head to Koukaki neighborhood for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a neighborhood café near your hotel — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, freddo espresso (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a souvlaki spot near the Acropolis Museum — pork souvlaki plate with pita, tomatoes, and tzatziki (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mani Mani restaurant in Koukaki — specializing in cuisine from the Mani peninsula with creative takes on traditional dishes (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Acropolis right at opening (8:00 AM) to avoid peak crowds and heat — temperatures can feel much hotter on the exposed hilltop by midday. Wear sunscreen and bring water. The combined Acropolis ticket is valid for 5 days and covers multiple sites.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion — take a KTEL bus from Pedion Areos park (€7 each way, ~2 hours) or join a shared tour. Visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60 meters above the Aegean Sea. Explore the ruins and enjoy breathtaking coastal views — Lord Byron carved his name into one of the columns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the small beach coves near Cape Sounion — Legrena Beach or Sounio Beach are within walking distance or a short taxi ride. Crystal-clear turquoise water, relatively uncrowded, and a perfect introduction to Greek beach life. Swim, snorkel, and relax on the pebble-and-sand shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by early evening. Relax and have a quiet dinner in the Kolonaki neighborhood — Athens' upscale but accessible district with excellent restaurants and a sophisticated atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee from a street vendor before catching the bus — quick and authentically Greek (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the taverna near the Temple of Poseidon — fresh grilled fish and Greek salad with a view of the temple (€18–25 per person, slightly touristy but worth the setting)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a bistro in Kolonaki — try lamb kleftiko (slow-cooked lamb) or fresh pasta with local ingredients (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check the KTEL bus schedule in advance — buses run roughly every 1–2 hours from Athens. The last bus back from Sounion is typically around 9:00 PM in summer. Bring a beach towel, sunscreen, and snorkeling gear if you have it. The temple is most magical in the late afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens for Santorini — take an early morning high-speed ferry from Piraeus Port (book in advance, ~5 hours, €40–60 with Seajets or Hellenic Seaways). Enjoy the scenic Aegean crossing with views of passing islands. Arrive in Santorini's Athinios Port and transfer to your accommodation in Fira or Oia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your Santorini accommodation (look for mid-range cave hotels or studios in Fira with caldera views). Explore Fira town — the island's capital — with its whitewashed buildings, blue-domed churches, and dramatic caldera views. Walk the scenic path from Fira toward Firostefani village.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Santorini sunset from Oia village — arrive by 7:00 PM to secure a good viewing spot at the castle ruins (Kastro). The sunset here is genuinely world-class. Afterward, browse Oia's boutique shops and art galleries.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the ferry or a quick bite at Piraeus Port before boarding
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Fira after arrival — a gyros or fresh salad at a café overlooking the caldera (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Oia after the sunset — try Roka restaurant or a similar mid-range spot with fresh seafood and local Santorinian fava (yellow split pea dip) and cherry tomato dishes (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance for June travel. High-speed ferries are faster but pricier; conventional ferries take 8+ hours but are cheaper. Book Santorini accommodation well in advance — the island fills up quickly in June. Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset — arrive early or consider the Imerovigli ridge as an alternative viewing spot.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the iconic Fira to Oia trail (10 km, ~3–4 hours) along the caldera rim — one of the most scenic walks in Greece. The path passes through Firostefani and Imerovigli villages with jaw-dropping caldera and volcano views. Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, reward yourself with a swim at one of Santorini's unique beaches. Head to Red Beach (near Akrotiri) — dramatic red volcanic cliffs and dark red sand — or Perissa/Perivolos Beach on the east coast with black volcanic sand, beach bars, and clear water. Relax and swim for 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the prehistoric ruins of Akrotiri — a Minoan Bronze Age settlement preserved under volcanic ash (often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean', €14 entry). Then enjoy dinner in the village of Megalochori or Pyrgos for a more authentic, less touristy Santorini experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a bakery in Fira before the hike — Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh fruit (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna lunch at Perivolos Beach — grilled octopus, fresh fish, and a cold Mythos beer (€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Metaxy Mas taverna in Exo Gonia — a beloved local restaurant known for authentic Santorinian cuisine, including fava, tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and grilled meats (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia hike is moderately challenging — wear proper shoes, bring 2+ liters of water, sunscreen, and a hat. The trail is well-marked but can be rocky. Red Beach has limited shade and can get crowded — arrive early. Akrotiri is best visited in the afternoon when morning tour groups have left.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour of the Santorini caldera — most tours depart from Fira's old port (accessible by cable car or donkey path). Visit the active Nea Kameni volcano and hike to the crater, then swim in the warm sulfuric hot springs at Palea Kameni. Tours typically run 4–5 hours (€25–40 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat tour and spend the afternoon exploring the medieval village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest point with a Venetian castle, traditional architecture, and panoramic island views. Browse local shops selling Santorinian wine, capers, and volcanic sea salt.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Santo Wines winery near Pyrgos for a sunset wine tasting — Santorini's volcanic soil produces unique Assyrtiko white wine with a distinctive mineral character. Tasting sessions with caldera views (€15–25 per person). Return to Fira for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Fira before the boat tour — spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat tour (often included) or grab a snack at the old port upon return
meals.dinner: Dinner at Argo restaurant in Fira — mid-range with excellent caldera views, fresh seafood pasta, and local wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the caldera boat tour the day before or in the morning — multiple operators depart from Fira's old port. The hot springs will stain light-colored swimwear orange due to the sulfur content — wear an older swimsuit. Santo Wines winery requires a reservation for sunset tasting sessions in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Santorini for Mykonos — take a high-speed ferry (approximately 2–3 hours, €35–55). Arrive in Mykonos Town (Chora) and check into your accommodation. Explore the iconic windmills of Kato Mili overlooking the harbor — the most photographed symbol of Mykonos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Mykonos Town's labyrinthine whitewashed alleys — designed to confuse pirates — discovering the famous Paraportiani Church, Little Venice waterfront, and colorful bougainvillea-draped streets. Visit the Archaeological Museum of Mykonos (€4) for island history.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Little Venice at sunset — the row of houses built directly over the sea with bars and cafés. This is one of the most romantic sunset spots in the Cyclades. Explore the lively Matogianni Street for shopping and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the ferry or a quick bite before departure in Santorini
meals.lunch: Lunch at a harbor-side café in Mykonos Town — fresh grilled fish or a Greek salad with local kopanisti cheese (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nikos Taverna in Mykonos Town — a beloved local institution serving fresh fish, lobster pasta, and traditional Greek dishes at reasonable prices for Mykonos (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is generally more expensive than other Greek islands — budget slightly more for meals and activities here. Book accommodation well in advance as June is peak season. The town's maze-like layout is intentional — embrace getting lost, as you'll discover hidden gems. Mykonos has a vibrant nightlife scene if that interests you.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short boat trip (30 minutes, €20 round trip) to the sacred island of Delos — one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the remarkably preserved ruins of this ancient religious center, including the iconic Terrace of the Lions, ancient temples, and mosaics. Boats depart from Mykonos Old Port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Delos and head to one of Mykonos' famous beaches. Platis Gialos is a good mid-range option with organized beach facilities, water sports, and clear water. Alternatively, take a water taxi to Paraga or Paradise Beach for a livelier atmosphere. Swim and relax for the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Explore the windmills area at golden hour for photos. Enjoy the famous Mykonos nightlife scene — start with cocktails at a Little Venice bar, then dinner, and optionally experience the island's legendary club scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a bakery in Mykonos Town before the Delos boat — Greek yogurt with local thyme honey (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or snack for Delos (no restaurants on the island, only a small café) — buy supplies from a Mykonos bakery beforehand
meals.dinner: Dinner at M-eating restaurant in Mykonos Town — creative Mediterranean cuisine with local ingredients, excellent wine list, mid-to-upper mid-range (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats run from approximately 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM — check the current schedule at the Old Port. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat as Delos has virtually no shade. The site is extensive — allow 2–3 hours to explore properly. The Delos entry fee is €12 in addition to the boat fare.

day_by_day.morning: Explore more of Mykonos' beaches — head to Elia Beach (the island's longest beach, accessible by bus or water taxi) for a more relaxed, less crowded morning swim. The water is crystal clear and the beach has a mix of organized sunbeds and free areas. Enjoy snorkeling in the calm morning waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos Town and visit the Folklore Museum housed in a traditional Mykonian sea captain's house — free entry, fascinating local artifacts and maritime history. Then explore the Aegean Maritime Museum (€4) with ship models and navigational instruments. Browse the boutique shops along Matogianni Street.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final Mykonos evening with a sunset cocktail at a Little Venice bar — Galleraki or Kastro Bar are iconic spots. Then a leisurely farewell dinner in Mykonos Town before an early night in preparation for tomorrow's travel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a beach café at Elia — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee with sea views (€10–14)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beach taverna at Elia Beach — grilled sea bream, Greek salad, and cold beer (€20–26 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Joanna's Nikos Place in Mykonos Town — a family-run taverna with generous portions of traditional Greek food at honest prices (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Elia Beach is accessible by KTEL bus from Mykonos Town (€2) or water taxi from Platis Gialos. The bus schedule can be irregular — check times in advance. This is a good day to do any last-minute souvenir shopping in Mykonos Town. Pack your bags in the evening for tomorrow's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mykonos for Crete — take a high-speed ferry or connecting flight (ferry ~5–6 hours to Heraklion, or fly via Athens ~1.5 hours total). Arrive in Heraklion, Crete's capital. Check into your accommodation and grab a quick lunch. Visit the impressive Heraklion Archaeological Museum (€15) — home to the world's finest collection of Minoan art and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos (€15, or €20 combined with the museum) — the legendary center of Minoan civilization, dating back 4,000 years. Explore the partially reconstructed palace complex with its famous frescoes, throne room, and labyrinthine layout (the inspiration for the myth of the Minotaur). Located just 5 km from Heraklion center.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's vibrant Lions Square (Plateia Venizelou) and the historic Venetian Loggia. Walk along the impressive Venetian harbor walls and visit the Koules Fortress (€4) for harbor views at dusk. Enjoy dinner in the lively restaurant district near the market street.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the ferry or at the airport — grab a Cretan dakos (barley rusk with tomato and cheese) from a café upon arrival (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the Archaeological Museum — a traditional Cretan meze plate with local cheeses, olives, and raki (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Peskesi restaurant in Heraklion — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant specializing in authentic Cretan cuisine using heirloom ingredients (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry or flight tickets well in advance. The high-speed ferry to Heraklion is scenic but long — bring entertainment. Knossos is best visited in the afternoon when morning tour groups have departed. The combined museum and Knossos ticket offers good value. Crete is the largest Greek island with a distinct culinary identity — prepare for exceptional food.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus west along Crete's northern coast to the charming Venetian harbor town of Chania (~2.5 hours by bus, €14, or rent a car for flexibility). Explore Chania's stunning old town — one of the most beautiful in Greece — with its Venetian lighthouse, colorful harbor, covered market, and narrow alleyways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Balos Lagoon — one of Greece's most spectacular beaches with turquoise shallow water and pink-tinged sand. Access by boat tour from Kissamos Port (€20 round trip, ~1.5 hours each way) or by 4WD vehicle via a rough dirt road. The lagoon is genuinely breathtaking — swim in the warm, shallow turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for the evening. Stroll along the Venetian harbor at sunset — the lighthouse and old buildings glow golden in the evening light. Explore the Splantzia neighborhood for a more local, less touristy atmosphere. Enjoy a Cretan dinner with local wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the bus or a quick stop in Rethymno — Cretan honey pie (melopita) and coffee (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for Balos Lagoon — buy supplies (local cheese, bread, olives, fruit) from Chania's covered market in the morning
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tamam restaurant in Chania's old town — housed in a converted Turkish bathhouse, serving creative Cretan-Mediterranean cuisine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Balos boat tour is the easiest way to reach the lagoon — book at Kissamos Port in the morning (boats typically depart at 10:30 AM and 12:30 PM). If renting a car, the dirt road to Balos requires a high-clearance vehicle. Balos can get crowded by midday — the boat tour timing works well. Stay overnight in Chania if possible for a more relaxed experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Crete — hike the famous Samaria Gorge if energy levels allow (16 km, 5–7 hours, €5 entry — one of Europe's longest gorges, ending at the Libyan Sea). Alternatively, for a more relaxed final morning, visit Elafonisi Beach near Chania — a stunning pink-sand beach with shallow turquoise water, accessible by bus (€5 each way).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the final afternoon swimming and relaxing at Elafonisi or the beach at the end of Samaria Gorge (Agia Roumeli). Soak in the last of the Greek sun and sea. Return to Heraklion or Chania airport depending on your departure flight — allow 2–3 hours for the journey and airport procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Crete. If your flight is late evening, enjoy a final Greek dinner at the airport or a nearby taverna. Reflect on 13 incredible days of ancient history, stunning beaches, and unforgettable food across Athens, Santorini, Mykonos, and Crete.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — Cretan graviera cheese, local honey, fresh bread, and strong Greek coffee at a harbor café in Chania (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beach taverna at Elafonisi — fresh grilled fish, horiatiki salad, and a cold Cretan beer (€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a taverna near the airport or in Heraklion — order a final spread of Cretan mezedes: dakos, staka (Cretan butter), and lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens) (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If doing the Samaria Gorge hike, start very early (buses from Chania depart at 6:15 AM) and wear proper hiking shoes — it's a serious but rewarding trek. The gorge is one-way, ending at Agia Roumeli, from where you take a boat to Hora Sfakion and then a bus back to Chania. Elafonisi is the more relaxed alternative. Confirm your return flight details and airport transfer well in advance. Allow extra time at Greek airports during peak summer season.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera, stopping at the Red Beach and White Beach for swimming and snorkeling. The evening departure lets you enjoy the world-famous Oia sunset from the water while avoiding the intense midday heat. Light snacks and local wine are typically included. Indoor alternative: visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira if weather turns.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches enclosed by towering white cliffs. Arrive before the crowds and midday heat for the best experience. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and explore the famous rusted shipwreck. Indoor alternative: visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos in the afternoon.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete
experiences.description: Join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and kalitsounia (cheese pastries) using locally sourced ingredients. Enjoy your creations for lunch with local raki. Held indoors or under shaded pergolas, ideal for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach at sunrise or early morning when the lagoon is calm, uncrowded, and the light is magical. Snorkel through the shallow turquoise lagoon teeming with sea life and explore the small islet connected by a sandbar. Rent snorkel gear locally for a minimal cost. Indoor alternative for midday: explore the nearby Chrysoskalitissa Monastery, a cool stone structure with cultural significance.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your five-star hotel in the Kolonaki or Syntagma district of Athens. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll around Syntagma Square and the National Garden to acclimate to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first evening with a sunset walk up Lycabettus Hill for panoramic views of Athens. Descend for a sophisticated welcome dinner at a top Athens restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in transit
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in transit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hytra (1 Michelin star, rooftop views of the Acropolis) — savor modern Greek cuisine with tasting menus featuring local ingredients and fine Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer. Confirm hotel early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — join a private or small-group guided tour of the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, spices, and local delicacies with a knowledgeable local guide. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up premium pantry souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon with a private licensed archaeologist guide for an in-depth, crowd-beating experience. Afterward, explore the Acropolis Museum at your own pace, marveling at original friezes and ancient artifacts in a world-class setting.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for boutique shopping and aperitifs at a rooftop bar. Enjoy a refined dinner showcasing modern Greek gastronomy.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full Greek spread with honey, yogurt, pastries, fresh fruit, and eggs
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch at Tzitzikas kai Mermigas in Monastiraki — creative Greek small plates in a charming setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside (1 Michelin star) — celebrated seafood-focused tasting menu by chef Lefteris Lazarou, set along the Piraeus waterfront

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and private guide well in advance. The food tour is best enjoyed on an empty stomach — eat lightly before.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the National Archaeological Museum — one of the world's great museums, housing the Mask of Agamemnon, Antikythera Mechanism, and extraordinary ancient Greek art. Arrange a private curator-led tour for a premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport for a short domestic flight to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 45 minutes). Upon arrival, collect your pre-arranged luxury rental car or private transfer and check in to your five-star resort (e.g., Blue Palace Elounda or Domes of Elounda). Spend the afternoon settling in and enjoying the resort's private beach and infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop bar overlooking the Aegean. Enjoy a leisurely dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Athens hotel — à la carte with fresh-squeezed juices, Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, and pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport lounge or a quick bite at a Heraklion harbor taverna upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant — Cretan-inspired cuisine featuring locally sourced ingredients, fresh seafood, and premium Cretan wines

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flight Athens–Heraklion in advance. Domes of Elounda or Blue Palace Elounda are exceptional luxury choices in Crete. Confirm resort transfer from Heraklion airport.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete — join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos, lamb with stamnagathi, and loukoumades using fresh local produce, olive oil, and herbs. Enjoy the meal you've prepared as part of the class.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient Minoan Palace of Knossos with a private archaeologist guide — explore Europe's oldest civilization and the legendary labyrinth of King Minos. Afterward, browse the charming streets of Heraklion's old town and visit the Venetian Koules Fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a spa treatment (book in advance) — try a traditional Cretan olive oil massage or thalassotherapy. Dine at a waterfront restaurant in Elounda village.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the cooking class
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during the cooking class — a true farm-to-table Cretan feast
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ferryman Taverna in Elounda — legendary waterfront seafood restaurant beloved by locals and discerning travelers alike

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 9:00–13:00. Book in advance through the resort concierge. Knossos is best visited in the afternoon when morning crowds thin.

day_by_day.morning: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach — depart at sunrise for the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach (approximately 1.5 hours from Elounda by car). Arrive early when the shallow turquoise lagoon is calm and nearly deserted. Snorkel the crystal-clear waters, explore the pink-tinged shoreline, and enjoy the magical morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the scenic western Crete coastline on the drive back, stopping at the charming Venetian harbor town of Rethymno. Wander the old town's narrow alleys, visit the Venetian Fortezza, and browse artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private sunset dinner on your villa terrace or balcony arranged by the resort concierge — a romantic in-room dining experience with Aegean views.

meals.breakfast: Pack a gourmet picnic breakfast from the resort to enjoy at Elafonissi Beach at sunrise
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional taverna in Rethymno old town — try fresh grilled octopus, fried calamari, and local Cretan cheeses
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining experience arranged by the resort — curated Cretan tasting menu with local wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is approximately 75 km from Elounda — depart by 5:30–6:00 AM to arrive at sunrise. Bring snorkeling gear (or rent at the beach). The drive through the White Mountains is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort — enjoy the private beach, infinity pool, and world-class spa facilities. Optional: sunrise yoga session on the clifftop terrace (arrange with the resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private boat charter from Elounda to the mysterious island of Spinalonga — the last active leper colony in Europe, now a haunting and fascinating UNESCO-listed historical site. Explore with a private guide, then cruise the surrounding turquoise waters and swim in secluded coves.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Crete at a top restaurant in Agios Nikolaos, the chic lakeside town near Elounda.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant overlooking the bay
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the boat during the Spinalonga cruise — arrange a catered picnic with the charter company
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pelagos Restaurant in Agios Nikolaos — acclaimed seafood restaurant with exceptional fresh catch and Cretan wine list

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charter to Spinalonga can be arranged through the resort concierge. The island closes to visitors in the evening — plan the afternoon visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Crete resort. Transfer to Heraklion Airport for a short domestic flight to Santorini (Thira Airport). Upon arrival, transfer via private car or cable car to your luxury caldera-view hotel in Oia or Imerovigli (e.g., Canaves Oia Epitome, Grace Hotel Santorini, or Andronis Luxury Suites).
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into your clifftop suite with breathtaking caldera views. Explore the iconic blue-domed village of Oia on foot — browse art galleries, jewelry boutiques, and artisan shops along the narrow whitewashed lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Oia's world-famous sunset from the castle ruins — arrive early to secure a prime spot. Afterward, enjoy a celebratory dinner at one of Santorini's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Crete resort before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Oia upon arrival — try local tomato fritters (tomatokeftedes) and fava dip
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Andronis Luxury Suites — Michelin-recommended, dramatic caldera views, exceptional modern Greek cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Heraklion to Santorini flights are approximately 40 minutes. Alternatively, a high-speed ferry (2 hours) is a scenic option. Book Santorini accommodation well in advance — luxury caldera properties sell out months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera — join a private or small-group luxury catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera. Stop at the iconic Red Beach (dramatic red volcanic cliffs), swim in the warm Aegean, and visit the hot springs near Nea Kameni volcanic island. Enjoy snorkeling in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — Santorini's remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Explore with a private guide. Afterward, visit the black-sand beach of Perissa or Perivolos for a relaxed swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the legendary sunset, this time from a private terrace or rooftop bar. Enjoy a wine tasting of Santorini's unique Assyrtiko wines at a premium winery.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — enjoy on your private terrace with caldera views
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served on the catamaran — fresh salads, grilled meats, local cheeses, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos — one of Santorini's most celebrated restaurants, showcasing the island's volcanic terroir through innovative Cycladic cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter in advance — sunset cruises are extremely popular. The catamaran experience can be timed for either morning or afternoon depending on preference.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Santo Wines Winery for a private morning wine tasting — perched on the caldera rim with spectacular views, taste Santorini's distinctive volcanic wines including Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto dessert wine. Learn about the island's unique basket-trained vine cultivation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the medieval village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest point, offering 360-degree island views. Visit the Byzantine castle ruins and charming artisan workshops. Alternatively, enjoy a private helicopter tour of the caldera and surrounding islands (arrange through the hotel concierge).
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a couples' or solo spa treatment at your hotel's luxury spa — try a volcanic stone massage or a wine therapy treatment unique to Santorini. Enjoy a final caldera-view dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, local honey, Santorini cherry tomatoes, and eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch at Metaxy Mas in Exo Gonia — beloved local taverna serving exceptional traditional Santorinian dishes in a rustic setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Argo Restaurant in Fira — stunning caldera views, fresh seafood, and an extensive Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: Santo Wines morning tastings are quieter and more intimate than afternoon sessions. Book the helicopter tour at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning in Santorini — enjoy a slow breakfast on your private terrace, take a dip in your infinity pool, and soak in the caldera views. Optional: sunrise hike from Fira to Oia along the caldera rim trail (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) for extraordinary early morning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry or private speedboat transfer from Santorini to Zakynthos (via Athens or direct charter, approximately 3–4 hours total). Check in to your luxury villa or boutique hotel on Zakynthos (e.g., a private villa in the Vassilikos peninsula area).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Zakynthos Town waterfront — stroll the Venetian-influenced harbor, visit the Byzantine Museum, and enjoy aperitifs at a waterfront café.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast in Santorini — enjoy every last caldera view moment
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Santorini port or on the ferry
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Zakynthos at Malanos Restaurant — a legendary local institution serving traditional Zakynthian cuisine with fresh seafood and local wines since 1949

day_by_day.notes: The Santorini–Zakynthos connection may require a connection through Athens or a private charter. Confirm routing and book well in advance. A private speedboat or seaplane charter is the most luxurious option.

day_by_day.morning: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip — take an early morning private boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed locations. Arrive before the crowds to swim in the impossibly blue enclosed bay, explore the rusting shipwreck, and enjoy the towering white limestone cliffs in golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion to the stunning Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos — snorkel in the electric-blue sea caves where sunlight refracts through the water creating an otherworldly glow. Return to the villa for a relaxed afternoon by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop viewpoint overlooking Navagio Beach (accessible by road from the top of the cliffs — a different and equally dramatic perspective). Enjoy a refined dinner at a top Zakynthos restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the villa or hotel before the boat departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on the private boat at Navagio Beach — fresh local produce, cheeses, charcuterie, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobelos Restaurant in Agios Nikolaos — elegant clifftop dining with panoramic Ionian Sea views and exceptional fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Porto Vromi by 7:00–7:30 AM to reach Navagio before the tour boats arrive. A private boat charter is strongly recommended for this experience. Bring sunscreen and water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Zakynthos Marine Park and Laganas Bay — home to the endangered loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta). Join a responsible wildlife boat tour to observe turtles in their natural habitat. The warm June waters make this an ideal time for sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Venetian-influenced Zakynthos Town in depth — visit the Church of Saint Dionysios (patron saint of the island), the Solomos Museum, and the elegant Plateia Solomou square. Browse local shops for Zakynthian specialties including mandolato nougat and local olive oil.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner on Zakynthos — enjoy a long, leisurely meal celebrating the penultimate night of the trip with the finest local cuisine and wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the villa — fresh local produce, Zakynthian honey, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional taverna in Keri village — try local specialties including bourdeto (spicy fish stew) and sofrito
meals.dinner: Dinner at Prosilio Restaurant in Zakynthos Town — sophisticated modern Greek cuisine in an elegant setting with an outstanding Greek wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The marine park turtle tours are strictly regulated — choose only certified eco-friendly operators. June is peak nesting season, making sightings highly likely.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at the villa, take a last swim in the Ionian Sea, and pack at a relaxed pace. Optional: visit the picturesque village of Keri and its lighthouse for sweeping views of the southern coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Zakynthos Airport (Dionysios Solomos Airport) for your departure flight back to Athens or directly to Belgrade. If time permits before the flight, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a waterfront café in Zakynthos Town.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Zakynthos, carrying memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring Greece's finest beaches, flavors, and ancient wonders.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the villa — a full spread of Greek favorites: yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a harbor café in Zakynthos Town — fresh salad, grilled fish, and a glass of local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Athens airport lounge or on the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and arrange private transfer to Zakynthos Airport. Allow at least 2 hours before departure. Consider purchasing local specialties as gifts: Zakynthian olive oil, mandolato, Santorini Assyrtiko wine, and Cretan thyme honey.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
